title: Open-extension unit normalization for derived tensor and base change
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes, let
$g:X'\to X$, and form $U'=U\times_X X'$ with $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and
$g_U:U'\to U$ [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. On the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $B_X,B_{X'}$ be sheaves of commutative rings
and $g^{-1}B_X\to B_{X'}$ a ring map; put $B_U=j^{-1}B_X$ and
$B_{U'}=j'^{-1}B_{X'}$, with the restricted structural ring map for $g_U$.
Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of these module sheaves
[def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
Use exact extension by zero $j_!,j'_!$ on the localized ringed sites
[def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact],
canonical derived module pullback and tensor
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the canonical
pullback-composition isomorphism $\theta:j'^*Lg^*\cong Lg_U^*j^*$.

The open adjunction units $u_M:M\to j^*j_!M$ and $u'_{M'}:M'\to j'^*j'_!M'$
are isomorphisms, in the normalization whose section over an object factoring
through the open is that same section. Extension by zero is fully faithful
on these derived categories. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$\beta_M:Lg^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*M,\qquad
\gamma_{M,N}:j_!M\otimes^L_{B_X}N\xrightarrow{\sim}
j_!(M\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*N).$$
Here $M\in D(B_U)$ and $N\in D(B_X)$ are arbitrary. The inverse of $\beta_M$
is the $j'_!\dashv j'^*$-adjunct of $Lg_U^*u_M$, followed by $\theta^{-1}$;
the inverse of $\gamma_{M,N}$ is the $j_!\dashv j^*$-adjunct of
$u_M\otimes1$ under the canonical restriction/tensor comparison. After the
open unit identifications, $j'^*\beta_M$ and $j^*\gamma_{M,N}$ are the
identity maps under these specified pullback and tensor identifications.
For constant finite $B_X=B_{X'}=A$, with the canonical constant-section structural ring map, these are precisely the canonical maps of
[lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] and
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. These assertions also hold for the ringed diagram topoi of arbitrary strict
inverse coefficient systems. More explicitly, use the site
$\mathbf N\times T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with topology generated by vertical
pro-etale covering families [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. A sheaf
of commutative rings on this site is an inverse system $B_{0,T}\leftarrow
B_{1,T}\leftarrow\cdots$; its module sheaves are the strict semilinear
module systems. Use their ordinary unbounded derived category, termwise
open extension, and total left derived system pullback and tensor.
The coefficient transitions and the structural ring maps are arbitrary;
no flatness or completion is imposed.

proof.text: Use the canonical pullback-map comparison on the Cartesian square and its product with the identity on the coefficient index. Its first-projection formula proves SiteSquare.first. Apply pushforwardNatIso to obtain the right square, whose section formula is reflexivity.

The existing independent-universe tensor-descent theorem supplies the homotopy resolving category and tensor localization. Whisker its representative isomorphism through the quotient comparison. ResolvingRepresentativeWhiskering proves the required descent property on complex representatives. Construct all four TensorModel records from these results.
Apply normalizedOperations_exists to those four tensor models and the explicit section-normalized right square. This produces the remaining geometric operation comparisons.

The ordinary section unit is the inverse of sectionIso. Localize its degreewise chain isomorphism using localization_unit_app and the exact-functor factorizations. Every derived object is isomorphic to Q of a complex, so both derived units are invertible. The adjunction theorem gives full faithfulness.

Construct beta inverse and gamma inverse by transposing the prescribed unit composites. Their adjuncts are isomorphisms. The two support lemmas put their targets in the essential images of the fully faithful open extensions, so the corresponding counits are isomorphisms. The adjunct formula f=F.map(adjunct f) followed by counit proves that these specific transposes are invertible. Componentwise invertibility gives natural isomorphisms.

For an isomorphism b:X to F(Y) whose inverse has adjunct e:Y to G(X), cancel e.hom and use the unit formula to prove G.map(b.hom)=e.inv followed by unit. Instantiate this with the pullback/unit composite and with the tensor/unit composite. These are precisely both restriction formulas; neither support lemma assumes any normalization.

Specialize exists_normalized to the finite constant input to obtain t, o and a. Construct the finite comparisons independently by [lem-sf-finite-comparisons-existence], then apply [lem-sf-finite-compatibility-transport] to the resulting e and a. Return t, o, a, e and the two canonical route equations. The original finite specialization statement is unchanged.

old_proof.text: By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the two open sites are the localized sites, and the open objects are subterminal: an object has at most one map to the open. Thus [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] restricts over the open to the original module sheaf, with its original restriction maps and scalar action. By [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification], applied to underlying abelian presheaves, restriction to the slice commutes with sheafification, compatibly with the sheafification units; module sheafification is abelian sheafification with its unique extended action [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], so the same holds for module sheaves; since the restricted presheaf is already the sheaf $M$, the restriction of $j_!M=P_M^\#$ is $M$ itself. The unit is precisely the inclusion of its unique summand, hence is the identity on these sections. This proves the unit isomorphisms for both $j$ and $j'$. The exact adjunctions of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] act termwise on complexes and descend by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Their termwise units and counits also descend: naturality for a quasi-isomorphism gives naturality for its inverse, hence for every localized morphism; the triangle identities remain equalities after localization. They therefore define the derived adjunctions with the same invertible units. For $M_1,M_2$, adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!M_1,j_!M_2)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(M_1,j^*j_!M_2)$, and composing with $u_{M_2}^{-1}$ identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}(M_1,M_2)$. This proves full faithfulness; replacing $j,M_i,u$ throughout this Hom calculation by $j',M'_i,u'$ proves it for $j'_!$.

old_proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P\to M$ and $Q\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. First the restriction/tensor comparison: by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] a tensor of module sheaves is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor; since $\mathcal O_U(V\to U)=\mathcal O(V)$, the sectionwise tensor of $A,B$ restricts to the sectionwise tensor of $A|_U,B|_U$, and [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification] (as in Step 1) gives $(A\otimes_{\mathcal O}B)|_U\cong A|_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}B|_U$, sending $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$ on local sections. Let $\phi_{G,F}:j_!(G\otimes j^*F)\cong j_!G\otimes F$ be the natural isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], and let $a_{G,F}:j_!(G\otimes j^*F)\to j_!G\otimes F$ be the $j_!\dashv j^*$-adjunct of $u_G\otimes1:G\otimes j^*F\to j^*j_!G\otimes j^*F\cong j^*(j_!G\otimes F)$. It is natural in both variables because $u$, the comparison and the adjunction bijection are, and $j^*a_{G,F}\circ u_{G\otimes j^*F}=u_G\otimes1$ by definition of the adjunct. On local sections over the open it is $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$. It is an isomorphism: by the Hom calculation of Step 1, applied to the module-sheaf adjunction with its invertible unit, the endomorphism $\phi^{-1}_{G,F}\circ a_{G,F}$ of $j_!(G\otimes j^*F)$ is $j_!e$ for a unique $e$, and naturality of $u$ gives $u\circ e=j^*(\phi^{-1}_{G,F})\circ j^*a_{G,F}\circ u=j^*(\phi^{-1}_{G,F})\circ(u_G\otimes1)$, a composite of isomorphisms by Step 1; hence $e$, and so $a_{G,F}$, is invertible. (Its target lies in the essential image of $j_!$ by $\phi$; this is what makes an invertible restricted transpose suffice here.) Apply $a$ in bidegree $(p,q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $j_!$ commutes with the direct sums in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Naturality of $a$ gives compatibility with $d_P\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_Q$ separately, and consequently with their sum $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$. We obtain a chain isomorphism $j_!\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes j^*Q)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(j_!P\otimes Q)$. To check the models, the same identity with any acyclic complex $E$ gives $(j_!P)\otimes E\cong j_!(P\otimes j^*E)$: $j^*E$ is acyclic by exactness, $P\otimes j^*E$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $j_!$ preserves acyclicity. Thus $j_!P$ is K-flat. For each flat $P^p$, the functor $F\mapsto j_!P^p\otimes F\cong j_!(P^p\otimes j^*F)$ is a composite of exact functors, proving flatness by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The same calculation proves these assertions for $j'_!$. Restriction of $Q$ is flat-term K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. The localization equivalence and tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] now descend the chain isomorphism, natural in both model variables, to $\gamma^{-1}$. Since its adjoint on models is $u_P\otimes1$, its descended adjoint is $u_M\otimes1$, as asserted.

old_proof.text: First prove base change for module sheaves, with the given arbitrary structural ring map. The morphism of pro-etale sites is presented by $V\mapsto X'\times_XV$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its localization at $U$, under [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], is the morphism for $g_U$: for $V\to U$ the canonical identification $V\times_UU'\cong V\times_XX'$ fixes both projections and commutes with all arrows in $V$. The restricted ring map is exactly the stipulated ring map for $g_U$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] gives $t:j^*g_*\cong g_{U*}j'^*$ and $s:g_U^*j^*\cong j'^*g^*$. In the first comparison both values at $V\to U$ are sections on the just-identified fibre products, with the same restricted scalar action. The module adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] and open adjunctions give composite adjunctions $L_1=g^*j_!\dashv R_1=j^*g_*$ and $L_2=j'_!g_U^*\dashv R_2=g_{U*}j'^*$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Conjugating $t:R_1\cong R_2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] (with the two adjunctions exchanged) produces an isomorphism $c:L_2\to L_1$. Explicitly it is the map characterized, for every $F$, by $j'^*c_F\circ u'_{g_U^*F}=s_{j_!F}\circ g_U^*u_F$: under the two composite Hom bijections the sectionwise comparison $t$ just restricts sections on the identical fibre product, so the transpose is precisely the displayed restricted unit. This identifies the comparison with the specified open-unit transpose, and proves its invertibility independently of restriction. Now resolve $M$ by $P$ as in Step 2. There $j_!P$ is flat-term K-flat, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] makes $g^*j_!P$ and $g_U^*P$ valid derived models. Therefore the termwise isomorphism $c_P$ descends, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], to $\beta^{-1}:j'_!Lg_U^*M\to Lg^*j_!M$. On the same flat-term K-flat models, $s$ and its inverse give $\theta^{-1}$ and $\theta$: restriction and pullback preserve these models, so their underived composition comparison computes the derived one. The displayed equation consequently becomes $j'^*\beta_M^{-1}\circ u'_{Lg_U^*M}=\theta^{-1}_{j_!M}\circ Lg_U^*u_M$. This is exactly the adjunct formula in the statement. Multiplying this equality by $j'^*\beta_M$ and the inverse unit proves the restriction identity for $\beta$. Step 2 likewise gives $j^*\gamma^{-1}_{M,N}\circ u_{M\otimes^Lj^*N}=u_M\otimes1$ under the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Multiplying by $j^*\gamma$ and the inverse units gives its required identity. Naturality follows from the naturality of $s,t$, the Hom bijections, and model descent.

old_proof.text: For strict inverse ring systems, use [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]: the ordinary derived category of strict semilinear module systems is the homotopy category of the enhanced section model, evaluations detect equivalences, and exact open extension, derived coefficient extension, tensor, pullback composition and adjunction transposes have simultaneous evaluation-compatible models. Thus no claim that a level of a system K-injective is K-injective is needed. The open unit is termwise the section identity of Step 1, and its inverse respects transitions because restriction of that identity is the identity at the next level. For tensor, the maps in Step 2 on local simple tensors send $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$; applying a coefficient transition sends this to $\tau(x)\otimes\tau(y)$ in either order, so the maps commute with every transition, including nonflat transitions. For base change, the comparisons in Step 3 come from the fibre-product projections and the specified restricted coefficient maps. A coefficient transition followed by restriction of a section equals restriction followed by that transition, by naturality of each coefficient ring map. The section model in the cited node preserves these comparisons and their adjunction transposes, so the resulting system $\beta^{-1}$ evaluates to the map of Step 3. The system $\gamma^{-1}$ evaluates to that of Step 2. At every level these are isomorphisms, hence are isomorphisms of derived systems by evaluation detection. The two displayed restriction equations in Step 3 and naturality hold already in the simultaneous section models (units, tensors, composition, and transposition are preserved), so they hold for the systems themselves; equality of maps is not inferred just from levelwise detection of equivalences. For the constant quotient towers specifically covered by [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison], its comparisons with ordinary level adjunctions give these same units and counits. The arbitrary strict-ring-system assertion uses the more general section-model node, without imposing the complete-DVR and quotient hypotheses of that special comparison.
